text:
Alice Chen: weird one — QuickCard briefly shows the previous org's project when you switch orgs fast and then open the card. saw this in prod today, reproduced on prod-rc twice.

Alice Chen: steps to repro: 1) click org switcher -> 2) immediately open quickcard from sidebar -> 3) hover details.

Alice Chen: screenshot shows header X-Org: 101 but quickcard rendered project for org 42.

Morgan (oncall): pinging infra — is there any async prefetch in the quickcard path? :thinking_face:

Julian: there is a prefetch layer that primes /internal/quickcard with route-affinity headers. it uses a cache keyed by user+route. could be a race where header binding happens after cache write.

Leah: ugh, we changed the cache key last month to drop org for perf. that was intentional for shared widgets but maybe wrong for quickcard.

Priya (pm): severity? are customers seeing wrong data or is it UI-only transient?

Alice Chen: appears UI shows wrong project for ~200-700ms. not sure persisted anywhere. saw it in support ticket where customer reported seeing another team's snippet.

Julian: paste of relevant log lines:
```
[2026-03-21T15:07:10.102Z] req_id=abc123 idx=1 user=alice org=101 route=/quickcard prefetched=false
[2026-03-21T15:07:10.150Z] cache_write key=user:alice:route:/quickcard value={org:42,project:search-ui}
[2026-03-21T15:07:10.170Z] req_id=abc123 idx=2 user=alice org=101 route=/quickcard prefetched=true served_from_cache=true
```

Julian: looks like a stale value (org:42) got written while the request's org header was 101. cache key missing org means cross-org bleed.

Leah: i'm surprised this wasn't catched by our telemetry. adding an assertion to detect mismatched org in cache write/serve should help.

telemetry-bot: Alert: quickcard_org_mismatch spike +42% over baseline in us-east-1.

Morgan (oncall): can we mitigate without a full rollback? options: 1) include org in cache key (simple), 2) short-circuit prefetch for quickcard for now, 3) add server-side guard to verify cached entry org==request org before serving.

Leah: #3 is safest low-risk hotfix — add guard check and metric, deploy immediately. then follow-up to revert cache key change or add config to opt-in sharing.

Priya (pm): agree. we'd prefer minimal customer impact. roll forward guard then evaluate perf impact.

Julian: i'll open a tiny patch that checks cachedItem.org == request.org before returning. also emit a telemetry counter 'quickcard.cache.org_mismatch'.

Alice Chen: thanks. can we also add an e2e test for rapid org switch? flakey repro but worth a regression test.

Julian: yep adding a Jest test to simulate concurrent switching + fetch.

Morgan (oncall): deploying the guard to prod-rc now, will promote if green.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Morgan (oncall) — service=console-quickcard env=prod-rc commit=bf4a9c7

telemetry-bot: Metric emitted: quickcard.cache.org_mismatch=7 in last 5m (prod-rc).

Morgan (oncall): prod-rc looks stable, no user-facing mismatches in last 10m. promoting to prod in 5.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Morgan (oncall) — service=console-quickcard env=prod commit=bf4a9c7

Alice Chen: verified on prod after deploy — quickcard shows correct org on rapid switch, couldn't repro. thanks everyone :tada:

Priya (pm): follow-ups: (1) revert the cache key drop or make it conditional, (2) add a rollout note so PMs are aware of tradeoff, (3) schedule a short postmortem to decide long-term.

Leah: will file RFC for cache-sharing semantics and a small perf bench to quantify org-in-key cost.

Julian: PR linked: https://git.redwood/infraproj/console-quickcard/pull/432

Alice Chen: closing thread — open issues in tracker: RW-1024 (postmortem), RW-1025 (e2e test).
